newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Weak on ample supply, poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Weak on ample supply, poor demand.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was softer on Friday due to ample supplies and recent crude falls, traders said.
"Both paper and crude are so weak that the fuel oil market is really bearish now," said one independent.

Despite some anticipation that Chinese players, after being sidelined before the early February Chinese Lunar New Year, might re-enter the market in March, traders were not optimistic it would be bullish for Singapore.
"When China buys, it may buy from South Korea," said one trader, noting talk that Japanese traders might offer some March cargoes was adding to uncertainties.
Singapore's Trade Development Board (TDB) announced on Thursday a rise of 1.974 million barrels to 12.299 million barrels in residual fuel stocks, a nine-month high.

"This is not a surprise. Cargoes have been coming in from the Middle East and there has been no Chinese interest. The TDB data only reconfirmed the fact that the market is oversupplied," one trader said.
Maintenance turnarounds of two Singapore refineries -- Mobile and Singapore Refinery Co -- in March could help limit supples, some traders said.
"But with the unusual quietness from the Chinese side, the outlook is still pretty bearish," said one independent.
In addition, China has already covered most of its requirements for the first half of March, traders said.
Fuel oil swaps continued to weaken in the wake of the bearish TDB residual stock data on Thursday.
March and April swaps dropped to $97.00/$98.00 and $96.00/$97.00 respectively, compared with Thursday's $99.50/$100.50 and $98.5/$99.5.
The bunker market, which was active with healthy demand earlier this week, turned quiet for the second day on ample supplies with many shipowners expecting further price cuts.
